cards.title: Ratings core: RATING_SCALE, notchChange and notchCalculator (REQ-06-02) with unit tests
cards.context:
WHY: Credit analysts need the notch change between a previous and a current rating, and the Watchlist level (WL) it produces. This card builds the shared core that the Ind. 12 indicator (card T-02) uses. The repo has no code yet: only src/.gitkeep and test/.gitkeep, and package.json has scripts.test = 'node --test' and no dependencies. Read CLAUDE.md first. Plain Node 18+ ESM (.mjs), no npm dependencies, tests use node:test and node:assert/strict.

FILES: create src/ratings/notch.mjs and test/ratings/notch.test.mjs. Do not touch src/indicators, package.json or docs/ (docs/POC_Requirements_v0.2_EN.md must stay unedited).

CONTRACT: named exports only, exactly these three and nothing else, no default export.
1) RATING_SCALE: Object.freeze([...]) holding exactly these 19 strings, best first: 'AAA','AA+','AA','AA-','A+','A','A-','BBB+','BBB','BBB-','BB+','BB','BB-','B+','B','B-','CCC+','CCC','CCC-'. The array index is the rank. This is the only place the scale exists.
2) notchChange(previous, current): returns the integer indexOf(current) - indexOf(previous). Positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, 0 unchanged. Return +0, never -0: plain subtraction of equal indexes gives +0; do not negate or multiply by -1 anywhere. This is the ONLY function that looks up a rating's position and the only place ratings are validated.
   Validation per rating, by a private helper (e.g. rankOf(value)): if typeof value !== 'string' throw a RangeError; otherwise t = value.trim() and look t up in RATING_SCALE by exact, case-sensitive match; not found -> RangeError. The message must contain the value EXACTLY as passed: the original untrimmed string for strings, String(value) for non-strings. Build the message with String(value), e.g. 'Invalid rating: ' + String(value) -- NOT a template literal or '+' on the raw value (both throw TypeError on a Symbol). String(Symbol('x')) is 'Symbol(x)', String({}) '[object Object]', String(null) 'null'. Validate previous FIRST, then current; when both are invalid the error names previous only. Rejected: 'CC','C','D','SD','NR','Baa1','XYZ','bbb+','','   ',null,undefined,42,{},Symbol('x'). ' BBB+ ' is accepted. Exotic objects (null-prototype, throwing toString) are out of scope.
3) notchCalculator(previous, current): returns exactly { notches, direction, wl } (three keys). notches = notchChange(previous, current) (must call notchChange, never index the scale itself). direction: 'downgrade' if notches > 0, 'upgrade' if < 0, 'unchanged' if 0. wl comes from a separate, named, NOT exported pure helper (e.g. calculatorWl(notches)) with the Ind. 13 thresholds: notches <= 1 -> 0, === 2 -> 1, >= 3 -> 2 (capped at 2). The helper MUST carry a code comment saying it is INTENTIONAL that a 1-notch downgrade gives WL 0 here while Ind. 12 (countryRatingChangeWl in src/indicators/countryRating.mjs) gives WL 1. Errors from notchChange propagate unchanged: no try/catch, no null, no 0 fallback.

PURITY (AD-5): no I/O, no console, no Date, no Math.random, no process/env, no node:fs/net/http/process imports, no mutable module state. src/ratings never imports src/indicators.

CORRECTED EXAMPLE: the POC text says BBB+ -> BB+ is 2 notches / WL 1. That is WRONG. On this scale it is 3 notches / WL 2. No test may assert 2 notches for BBB+ -> BB+.

UNIT TESTS (test/ratings/notch.test.mjs, import from '../../src/ratings/notch.mjs'): pinned cases of AC-1..AC-10, the calculator part of AC-13 and the notch part of AC-14, as listed in the acceptance lines and the spec.
acceptance: AC-1 [P0]: Given `import { RATING_SCALE } from "../../src/ratings/notch.mjs"`, when it is read, then `assert.deepStrictEqual(RATING_SCALE, ["AAA","AA+","AA","AA-","A+","A","A-","BBB+","BBB","BBB-","BB+","BB","BB-","B+","B","B-","CCC+","CCC","CCC-"])` passes, `RATING_SCALE.length === 19` and `Array.isArray(RATING_SCALE) === true`.

AC-2 [P2]: Given `RATING_SCALE` in strict ESM code, when a caller tries to mutate it, then `Object.isFrozen(RATING_SCALE) === true`, and each of `RATING_SCALE.push("CC")`, `RATING_SCALE[0] = "X"` and `RATING_SCALE.length = 0` throws `TypeError`. Afterwards the array still deep-equals the AC-1 list.
AC-3 [P0]: Given two valid ratings, when `notchChange(previous, current)` is called, then it returns the integer `RATING_SCALE.indexOf(current) - RATING_SCALE.indexOf(previous)`.

AC-4 [P2]: Given the same rating twice, when `notchChange(r, r)` is called for each of the 19 steps (e.g. `notchChange("BBB","BBB")`), then the result is `0` and `Object.is(result, 0) === true` (never -0).

AC-5 [P0]: Given an invalid rating in either position, the other being `"BBB"`, when `notchChange` is called, then it throws an instance of `RangeError` and returns nothing. This applies to each of the 15 pinned values, in both positions (30 calls):
AC-6 [P2]: Given an invalid rating, when `notchChange` throws, then the `RangeError` message contains the value as it was passed:

AC-7 [P2]: Given a valid rating with surrounding spaces, when `notchChange(" BBB+ ", "BB+")` is called, then it returns `3`. `notchChange("BBB", " BBB ")` returns 0 with `Object.is(result, 0) === true`.
AC-8 [P1]: Given a previous and a current rating, when `notchCalculator(previous, current)` is called, then the result `deepStrictEqual`s, with exactly 3 keys:
AC-9 [P1]: Given all 361 ordered pairs `(p, c)` of `RATING_SCALE`, when `notchCalculator(p, c)` is called, then for every pair:

AC-10 [P2]: Given the same rating twice, when `notchCalculator("BBB","BBB")` is called, then it `deepStrictEqual`s `{ notches: 0, direction: "unchanged", wl: 0 }` and `Object.is(result.notches, 0) === true`.

AC-13 [P0], calculator part: Given an invalid rating, when `notchCalculator` is called, then the `RangeError` from `notchChange` propagates unchanged. The function returns no null, no 0, no object and no error object.

cards.title: Indicator 12: countryRatingChangeWl (REQ-03-12) on top of notchChange, with unit tests
cards.context:
WHY: Indicator 12 (country rating change, REQ-03-12, a Must) scores how far a client's country rating moved between a previous and a current rating, as a Watchlist level (WL 0-4, higher is worse; this rule only produces 0-2). It builds on the ratings core from card T-01. Read CLAUDE.md first. Node 18+ ESM (.mjs), no npm dependencies, node:test and node:assert/strict.

WHAT T-01 PROVIDES (src/ratings/notch.mjs, do NOT modify it): RATING_SCALE (frozen array of 19 strings: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-); notchChange(previous, current) -> signed integer (positive = downgrade, negative = upgrade, +0 = unchanged), throws RangeError on any invalid rating with the message containing the value as passed, previous checked first; notchCalculator(previous, current) -> {notches, direction, wl} with Ind. 13 thresholds.

FILES: create src/indicators/countryRating.mjs and test/indicators/countryRating.test.mjs. Nothing else. Do not edit package.json or docs/.

CONTRACT: exactly ONE named export, countryRatingChangeWl(previous, current), returning the number 0, 1 or 2. No default export, no other exports. Implementation: import { notchChange } from '../ratings/notch.mjs'; get the distance only by calling notchChange; do not copy the scale or a rating list; do no own validation or trimming. Apply a separate, named, unexported pure helper (e.g. ind12Wl(notches)): notches <= 0 -> 0, === 1 -> 1, >= 2 -> 2. The helper MUST carry a code comment saying it is INTENTIONAL that a 1-notch downgrade gives WL 1 here while notchCalculator in src/ratings/notch.mjs (Ind. 13 thresholds) gives WL 0. The RangeError from notchChange propagates unchanged (no try/catch, no null/0 fallback).

PURITY (AD-5): no I/O, console, Date, Math.random, process/env, node:fs/net/http/process imports, no module state. src/indicators may import src/ratings, never the reverse.

OUT OF SCOPE: no override/editable parameter, no public-source fetching, no Moody's mapping.

UNIT TESTS (test/indicators/countryRating.test.mjs; import RATING_SCALE, notchChange, notchCalculator from '../../src/ratings/notch.mjs' for the loop and cross-check): AC-11 table + 361-pair loop; AC-12 cross-check ('A','A-'); the indicator part of AC-13; the indicator part of AC-14.

SUITE (AC-16): after your tests pass, run 'npm test' from the worktree root; it must exit 0 and include both test files.

AC-17 NOTE: you do not write the PR; Michael does at ship. In your handoff list the text the PR must contain: (1) the consuming form job owns REQ-03-12 'auto-filled value editable'; (2) the consuming UI needs a mapping step because Moody's, CC, C, D, SD and NR throw RangeError; (3) the POC owner should correct the REQ-06-02 example to BBB+ -> BB+ = 3 notches / WL 2; (4) the reviewer lenses were skipped; plus the intentional 1-notch WL difference (calculator WL 0 vs Ind. 12 WL 1).

AC-12 [P1]: Given the 1-notch downgrade `("A","A-")`, when both functions are called, then `notchCalculator("A","A-").wl === 0` and `countryRatingChangeWl("A","A-") === 1`. The Ind. 12 helper in `countryRating.mjs` carries a code comment saying it is intentional that a 1-notch downgrade gives WL 1 here and WL 0 in `notchCalculator` (B-36; checked by review).
